chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated from Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from more than one person, from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon them both), who said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is more merciful to His creation than to compel them to commit sins and then punish them for them. And Allah is Mightier than intending a matter and it not coming to pass. He was asked (the two Imams): Is there a third position between compulsion (al-jabr) and free will (al-qadar)? They replied: Yes, and it is broader than what is between the heaven and the earth.

key_terms.القدر: Free will / Decree (often used for natural destiny or choice in this context)
key_terms.بين السماء والأرض: Between the heaven and the earth

ai.seo_question: What is the third position between compulsion and free will in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the matter between the two matters), rejecting both absolute determinism (*Jabr*) and total free will (*Tafwid*). The Imams emphasize that God’s mercy precludes forcing creation into sin, while His omnipotence ensures His will is never thwarted, establishing a middle ground where human agency operates within divine decree. This intermediate state is described as 'wider than the sky and the earth,' highlighting the vastness of the space where free choice and predestination coexist.
